svg.title: Newton’s laws & practical
svg.desc: First law & inertia: Zero resultant → rest or constant velocity. Inertia is the tendency to retain that motion. Balanced forces do not mean no forces. A steady car has driving force = resistance. Second & third laws: F = ma, using resultant F. Inertial mass = F/a. More mass → less a for same F. Third law: equal opposite forces of same type on different objects. Weight and normal force on one book are not a pair. Terminal velocity: Initially weight > drag → downward acceleration. Speed rises → drag rises → resultant and a fall. Drag = weight → constant terminal velocity. Opening parachute increases drag, slowing fall to a lower terminal speed. Measure acceleration: Low-friction trolley, string, pulley, hanging mass. Light gates or motion sensor measure velocity changes. Calculate a = Δv/Δt before hanger hits floor. Secure pulley; stop trolley safely; control friction. Vary force: Transfer masses from trolley to hanger: total moving mass constant, driving weight increases. For whole system, driving force ≈ hanger weight if friction negligible. Trolley tension alone is not hanger weight while accelerating. Vary mass: Keep hanging mass fixed; add mass to trolley. Force approximately constant, total mass increases. Repeat; a vs F should be proportional at fixed mass. a vs 1/m should be proportional at fixed force.
